memo.intro: First-look memo as of 2026-11-03. Public data only. Every factual sentence links to its source; a separate verifier removed unsupported claims. Paragraphs marked Analysis are the research agent's judgment, not cited fact.

sentences.text: Setuav/PyThrust is described as an open-source framework for electric propulsion system analysis and optimization in UAV design.
sentences.note: Source 65 description for Setuav/PyThrust matches exactly.

sentences.text: Setuav/Studio is described as a plugin-based desktop application for parametric UAV design and analysis.
sentences.note: Source 65 gives Studio's description as a plugin-based desktop application for parametric UAV design and analysis.

sentences.text: Setuav/mavlink2grpc is described as an ultra-fast, schema-first MAVLink to gRPC bridge and code generator for modern UAV communication.
sentences.note: Source 24 description matches word for word.

sentences.text: The evidence names no founders or employees, so we cannot judge team background, defense experience, or hardware depth.
PyThrust is written in Python and its topics include openmdao, scipy and optimization.
sentences.note: Source 65 lists language Python and topics openmdao, optimization, scipy for PyThrust.

sentences.text: The PyThrust tree has test files for autotune, battery, motors, propellers, solver and openmdao.
sentences.note: Source 316 notable paths include tests/test_autotune.py, test_battery.py, test_motors.py, test_propellers.py, test_solver.py, test_openmdao.py.

sentences.text: Studio's topics include aerosandbox, aerodynamics and weight-balance, and its tests include an AeroSandbox reference file.
sentences.note: Source 65 lists Studio topics aerosandbox, aerodynamics, weight-balance; source 330 lists tests/_aerosandbox_reference.py.

sentences.text: The Studio tree lists a packages/setuav-studio-sdk path and an example plugin.
sentences.note: Source 330 notable paths include packages/setuav-studio-sdk/ files and packages/example-plugin/README.md.

sentences.text: mavlink2grpc lists topics including ardupilot, px4, protobuf and cpp17, and its tree has 14 hardware-adjacent files.
sentences.note: Source 24 lists the topics ardupilot, px4, protobuf, cpp17; source 322 states 14 hardware-adjacent files.

sentences.text: The hard problem in propulsion modeling is accuracy of motor, propeller and battery models away from catalog operating points, where efficiency, thermal limits and battery sag rarely match datasheets.
Using OpenMDAO and SciPy is the standard open approach, so the novelty is likely packaging and usability, not new physics.
The hard problem in the design tool is coupling aerodynamics, weight and balance, and propulsion into one trustworthy loop.
Building on AeroSandbox and a plugin SDK is ordinary for the field, and its value depends on validation against flight test data, which the evidence does not show.
The MAVLink bridge addresses a real integration pain: companion computers speak MAVLink poorly to modern services.
Schema-first generation is a sensible but not unique idea, and the hard part is latency, reliability and message coverage across PX4 and ArduPilot dialects.
Open-source flight stacks like PX4 and ArduPilot are mature, and defense buyers now want cheap, fast-iterated small UAVs, so tooling that shortens design cycles for small teams has a clear pull.
The repositories were created in 2026, and the PyThrust forks cluster in early June, which suggests the launch drew a burst of interest from developers during that window.
Python scientific tooling and optimization frameworks such as OpenMDAO make it cheap for a small team to ship credible design software, which lowers the barrier compared with older proprietary tools.
Studio has 45 pull requests on the fetched page from people outside the owning organization, dated 2026-08-27 to 2026-10-28.
sentences.note: Source supports 45 PRs from outside the org dated 2026-08-27 to 2026-10-28 (on this page). The claim that this shows contributor activity but not paying demand is an inference not in the text.

sentences.text: PyThrust has a permissive-looking open source setup with a LICENSE file, so direct payment for the core library is unlikely.
Likely payers are drone makers, defense integrators and university labs that want supported design tools, integrations or custom models, but the evidence shows no customers or pricing.
PyThrust was created on 2026-05-26 and the earliest releases on the fetched page are dated 2026-06-02.
sentences.note: Creation date 2026-05-26 is supported and the earliest releases are dated 2026-06-02 (two on that date). Wording 'first releases' is fine, so this is basically matched; however the release list is only 'on this page', so completeness of 'first' is not confirmed.

sentences.text: mavlink2grpc was created on 2026-06-06 and had two releases dated 2026-06-07.
sentences.note: Source 24 gives created_at 2026-06-06; source 320 shows 2 releases both dated 2026-06-07.

sentences.text: mavlink2grpc was last pushed on 2026-06-18.
Studio was created on 2026-08-15 and had three releases on the fetched page, two dated 2026-08-29 and one dated 2026-09-16.
sentences.note: Creation date 2026-08-15 supported; releases dated 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-16 are listed, but source shows 3 releases (two on 2026-08-29).

sentences.note: Source 314 latest release date is 2026-09-08 and source 65 pushed_at is 2026-09-08.

sentences.text: Studio was last pushed on 2026-10-28.
As of 2026-11-02, PyThrust had 153 stars and 23 forks, Studio had 4 stars, and mavlink2grpc had 31 stars and 5 forks.
sentences.note: Sources 65 and 24 (fetched 2026-11-02) give PyThrust 153 stars and 23 forks, Studio 4 stars, mavlink2grpc 31 stars and 5 forks.

sentences.text: Technical risk: if the propulsion models are not validated against measured thrust and battery data, engineers will not trust the optimizer output, and the tools become demos.
Commercial risk: the core tools are free and open, and defense buyers usually pay for qualified, supported, often export-controlled systems, so a free design library may never convert to revenue.
Competition risk: established tools such as AeroSandbox, OpenMDAO-based projects and commercial propulsion calculators can add similar features, and the bridge competes with existing MAVLink SDKs.
Team risk: with no named people and mavlink2grpc idle since June, the effort may be a side project that lacks sustained engineering or a defense go-to-market.
The public record does not show who founded Setuav, whether it is a funded company, or whether it has any customers.
It does not show whether the models were validated with flight or bench tests, or whether any hardware product is planned.
It is unclear how much of the outside pull request activity is real users versus one-off contributions.

founder_call_questions: Who is on the team, and what are your backgrounds in UAV design and defense?
How have you validated PyThrust motor, propeller and battery models against bench or flight data?
What accuracy do you see in predicted thrust, efficiency and endurance versus measurements?
What is the business model given the tools are open source, and what would a customer pay for?
Do you have any paying or pilot customers, and are they defense, commercial or academic?
Why did mavlink2grpc stop receiving pushes after June, and is it still part of the plan?
What is the Studio plugin SDK strategy, and who writes plugins?
Who are the outside contributors to Studio, and are they users or paid collaborators?
How do you handle export control and security needs for defense users of open design tools?
Is there a hardware product on the roadmap, or is Setuav staying a software company?
